plan.strategy_summary: The strategy goes long when the fast moving average exceeds the slow moving average, based on the prior day's crossover, and only on weekdays selected from a predefined set. It selects the fast/slow lengths and weekday combination that historically yielded the highest Sharpe ratio.

findings.snippet: return max(PARAM_GRID, key=lambda p: run_backtest(prices, positions_for(prices, **p)).metrics["sharpe"])
findings.explanation: Parameter search uses the full history to pick the best configuration, causing look‑ahead bias in the selected parameters.
Uses the parameters chosen on the entire sample.

test_plan.hypothesis: Sharpe will remain similar because the strategy already shifts its signal by one bar, so an additional shift only moves to older information.
Because parameters are chosen using the full history, truncating the data changes the best parameters and thus the position at time t.

The walk‑forward test will select parameters on the first 60% and evaluate on the remainder, but the strategy instead uses parameters chosen on the entire sample, leading to out‑of‑performance degradation.
With ~280 parameter combinations, the deflated Sharpe will penalize the Sharpe and typically produce a warning even on random‑walk data.

tests.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 week (same weekday) barely changed results (Sharpe 0.52 -> 0.47). The strategy only trades on Mon, so each trade was delayed to the same weekday a week later.
On 4 of 12 dates, the position changed when future data was hidden: the strategy uses information that wasn't available at decision time.
The best configuration on past data (Sharpe 0.76) fell to 0.18 on data it hadn't seen: the edge doesn't survive out of sample.
After accounting for 279 configurations tried, there's only a 17% chance the edge is real -- the best of that many random tries would look this good by luck.

report.headline: The strategy’s reported returns cannot be trusted because it looks ahead and overfits its parameters.

tests.explanation: Delaying the signal by one week (same weekday) barely changed performance (Sharpe 0.52 → 0.47), showing the strategy only trades on Mondays and any lag simply moves trades to the same weekday a week later.
On 4 of 12 dates the position changed when future data was hidden, meaning the strategy used information that was not available at decision time when it selected its parameters.
The best parameter set found on past data (Sharpe 0.76) dropped to 0.18 on unseen data, indicating the edge does not generalize out of sample.
After accounting for the 279 parameter combinations tried, there is only a 17% chance the observed Sharpe ratio is genuine; the result could easily arise by luck.

fixes.fix: Replace the global parameter search with a rolling or expanding‑window selection so that best_params uses only data available up to each prediction point (e.g., compute parameters on an expanding window or use a walk‑forward scheme).

report.caveats: This audit relies on the supplied synthetic data and the deterministic tests implemented in the engine; a WARN would indicate ‘not proven’ rather than ‘broken’, and passing tests do not guarantee future performance in live markets.
